Abstract: In the process of energy transition, the integration of non-fossil energy sources and the associated measures within the energy transmission grid represent an infrastructural challenge. High-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission plays a crucial role in reducing transmission losses. Under HVDC stress and/or pulses, the insulation medium air loses its dielectric strength, which manifests itself in electrical discharges. These local discharges lead to electrical breakdowns in high-voltage systems and damage components. To prevent this, conductive components with different electrical potentials have to be spatially separated. A prerequisite for a corresponding breakdown is the formation of a conductive plasma (streamer). If this exceeds a certain limit temperature, a breakdown is to be assumed. The formation of the plasma or an ionizing channel is usually modelled by coupling the Poisson equation with a transport equation for the charge particles involved. Of particular importance is the numerical calculation of DC voltages which are superimposed with new slow front pulses occurring in HVDC. Due to the high electric fields over different orders of magnitude, there are special requirements for the solution method. In order to guarantee the important particle preservation in conservative systems, a flux-correcting method such as the discontinuous-Galerkin method is used for the numerical solution.
